title: CoForge run record
description: Defined BEFORE measuring, so measurements are not invented ad hoc — the same argument as the component contract schema (ADR-013). PRIVACY: counts and identifiers only. No conversation content, no file contents, no free text. Enforced by a self-check in collect-metrics.py. Every property below carries a written definition (C-057, 2026-09-08) because a number whose definition is not written down cannot be compared across runs — the ADR-014 argument, extended from 'has a schema' to 'every field in the schema is defined', after two fields (gates.source, corrections.with_check/unchecked) were found emitted by the collector but absent from this schema — meaning nothing here was ever actually validated against what gets written.

run_id.description: ISO date the record was generated FOR. One record per calendar day; re-running the collector on the same day overwrites that day's file (idempotent), it never creates a second file for the same date.

generated_at.description: ISO timestamp the collector actually ran, local time. Can differ from run_id's date only if the collector is run after midnight for the previous day's close-out.

project.description: os.path.basename of the repository root at collection time — an identifier, not a path.

provenance.description: Present ONLY on records written schema_version 2 (2026-09-08) or later. ITS ABSENCE IS THE MARKER for a pre-fix record: those records summed every raw transcript file in ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl, including nested conversation forks that are supersets of one another, and are inflated by roughly 2.1x on this project's corpus (C-057). Never backfilled onto old records — that would let a guessed method stand in for a measured one, which is the defect this field exists to prevent. See validation/reports/2026-09-08__collector-dedup-fix.md.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS schema file the record was written against. '2' = uuid-deduplicated counting (2026-09-08 onward). No 'schema_version 1' value was ever stamped — version 1 records are recognisable only by having no provenance block at all.

counting_method.description: Machine-readable tag for how transcript records were aggregated. 'uuid-dedup-v1': every record is keyed by its message uuid when present, else by a sha256 of its own canonical JSON, and only the first occurrence of a key is counted — so a record appearing in several overlapping transcript files (a session and its forks) contributes exactly once.

detail.description: Pointer to where the full prose definition of counting_method lives — validation/metrics.schema.json (this file) and validation/reports/2026-09-08__collector-dedup-fix.md. Kept short deliberately: the privacy check refuses any record value that reads as prose, so definitions live in the schema/report, never inlined into the record itself.

session.description: Facts about the transcript corpus itself, all computed AFTER de-duplication (see provenance). Pre-schema_version-2 records instead carry a single ambiguous 'duration_min' field (first-timestamp-to-last-timestamp across the WHOLE multi-day range, not de-duplicated) — retired, not reused, because it answered neither of the two questions defined below.

turns.description: Count of DE-DUPLICATED transcript records that carry a `usage` block — i.e. one model completion with token accounting, counted once even if it appears in multiple nested transcript files.

transcripts.description: Count of *.jsonl FILES read in ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/. This is a file count, not an event count, and is NOT de-duplicated — nested forks each count as one file even though their contents overlap. Use unique_records for the de-duplicated event count.

unique_records.description: Count of distinct de-duplication keys (uuid, or content-hash for records with no uuid) seen across ALL transcript files combined. This is the true number of distinct events; it is smaller than the sum of each file's own record count whenever any file is a fork of another.

non_message_records.description: Of unique_records, how many are session/UI bookkeeping events with no uuid and no usage block (queue-operation, custom-title, mode, ai-title, atis-latch, bridge-session, frame-link, artifact-*-ledger). Verified empirically (2026-09-08, this project's corpus) that none of these ever carry token usage, so they are excluded from turns/tokens/tools without loss. Reported here so that exclusion is visible, not silent.

active_minutes_distinct.description: Count of distinct UTC calendar-minutes (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM) in which at least one de-duplicated record carries a timestamp. A LOWER BOUND on time spent: a minute with ten records and a minute with one record both count as 1, and it never counts a minute nothing happened in.

active_hours_distinct_minutes.description: active_minutes_distinct / 60, rounded to 1 decimal. One of the two DEFINED 'how long was this session' readings — the smaller one, because it counts only minutes with recorded activity.

elapsed_span_by_day_hours.description: Group de-duplicated timestamps by UTC calendar day; for each day take (latest timestamp − earliest timestamp) in hours; sum across all days present. The OTHER defined 'how long' reading — an UPPER BOUND, because it counts every gap WITHIN a day (a lunch break, a long pause) as active time. Does NOT count the overnight gap between days, so it is smaller than a single first-to-last span over the whole multi-day range would be. On this project's 2026-09-08 corpus this reads ~151.1h against ~32.0h for active_hours_distinct_minutes — both correct, answering different questions.

duration_min.description: LEGACY, schema_version < 2 only. First-timestamp-to-last-timestamp across the ENTIRE multi-day range (not per-day, not de-duplicated), in minutes. Retired because it is a third, more ambiguous reading than either active_hours_distinct_minutes or elapsed_span_by_day_hours and was never named as such. Not emitted by schema_version 2+.

tokens.description: Billable = input + output. Cache figures reported separately because they dominate volume but not cost. Schema_version 2+: summed over DE-DUPLICATED transcript records only (see provenance) — pre-fix records summed every transcript file including nested forks and are inflated roughly 2.1x on this project's corpus.

input.description: Sum of input_tokens across de-duplicated turns.

output.description: Sum of output_tokens across de-duplicated turns.

cache_read.description: Sum of cache_read_input_tokens across de-duplicated turns. Dominates volume, excluded from billable.

cache_creation.description: Sum of cache_creation_input_tokens across de-duplicated turns. Excluded from billable.

billable.description: input + output only. The figure comparable to invoiced cost; cache figures are reported alongside but not folded in.

tools.description: tool name → call count. One call per tool_use content block on a de-duplicated turn; a tool_use block belonging to a record already counted (via an overlapping transcript fork) is not re-counted.

skills.description: skill name → activation count, drawn from the Skill tool's `skill` input on de-duplicated turns only.

artifacts.description: Snapshot of artifacts/_registry.json at collection time — not derived from transcripts, not subject to the de-duplication fix.

total.description: Count of all entries in _registry.json regardless of status.

live.description: total minus entries with status superseded or archived.

tokens_per_artifact.description: billable tokens / artifacts.total, rounded. null when total is 0 (never divide by zero silently).

gates.description: skipped is tracked as a first-class outcome — skipped is not passed. Derived by RUNNING validation/audit-system.py --json live at collection time, never by parsing a report file (C-026).

verdict.description: Overall audit verdict string (e.g. PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED) as returned by the live audit run, or UNKNOWN/UNAVAILABLE on failure to run.

blocker.description: Count of blocker-severity findings from the live audit run. null (not 0) if the audit could not be run — zero is a measurement, null is an admission it wasn't taken.

error.description: Count of error-severity findings. null if the audit could not be run.

warning.description: Count of warning-severity findings. null if the audit could not be run.

info.description: Count of info-severity findings. null if the audit could not be run.

skipped.description: Count of checks the audit itself reported as skipped (not passed). null if the audit could not be run.

source.description: 'live-audit' if validation/audit-system.py --json was actually invoked and returned successfully this run; 'unavailable' if the subprocess call failed or timed out. Set to 'live-audit' ONLY after the subprocess returns, never before — a marker set before the thing it attests to has happened is the same defect as a value nothing applies to.

corrections.description: Snapshot of validation/corrections.json at collection time (not memory/corrections.md, which is gitignored and would read 0 in a fresh clone — C-026).

logged.description: Total entries in the ledger. null if the ledger file could not be read.

with_check.description: Entries carrying a non-empty `check` field naming the validator that would catch the defect again.

unchecked.description: Entries with no `check` field — a found-and-fixed defect with no third leg (SR: 'found and fixed is two of three').

source.description: Always 'validation/corrections.json' — recorded so a reader never has to guess which of the two 'corrections.md' files in this repo produced the count.

governance.description: Simple file-count facts about the repo's own governance surface, not derived from transcripts.

artifact_types.description: The `count` field from artifacts/_types.json — the number of registered artifact types.

readiness.description: Percentages parsed from a live run of validation/readiness-audit.py. Empty object ({}) if that run failed — absence, not zero, on failure.

l1.description: L1 Foundations readiness percentage, as reported by readiness-audit.py.

l2.description: L2 Complete readiness percentage, as reported by readiness-audit.py.

workflow.description: Workflow readiness percentage, as reported by readiness-audit.py.
